                    ### Question

Participant C is strapped in a supine position on a bed in a horizontal orientation. Blood pressure readings are then taken at the level of the head, heart, and feet from all 3 participants. Which of these positions will have the lowest recorded blood pressure reading?

opb. Participant B: at the level of the feet

For Participant A, who is upside down, the head is lower than the heart, leading to increased hydrostatic pressure and higher blood pressure at the head. For Participant B, who is oriented with the head higher than the heart, the hydrostatic pressure is decreased at the head, resulting in lower blood pressure readings there. Participant C, in a horizontal position, experiences a more uniform hydrostatic pressure distribution, leading to normal blood pressure readings at the heart. Therefore, the lowest recorded blood pressure reading is expected at Participant B's head, where the hydrostatic pressure is reduced due to the head being higher than the heart.
